label: first occurrence of 0/m/z/b (and weaker u/w/s/q) during the input phase
explanation: Input-phase token detector: 98% of activation mass is on original-token steps; almost silent on <DEL> and copy steps. Strongest when the input is 0, m, z or b (rate ~25%, about 5x lift, ~61% of mass together), weaker for u, w, s, q, f, p (rate 6-11%). Mostly the first occurrence of the token (94% of mass has in_first=1). Rate is highest early in the sequence (t=0-3, 10-14%) and drops after t=4. Even for the preferred tokens it fires on only about a quarter of occurrences, depending on preceding context in ways this predicate does not capture: top activations often follow e/t/q/f, and the unit is less likely to fire once another preferred token has already been seen. Magnitude is graded across the preferred tokens; the top examples are mostly 0, m, z, q, u. The predicate gets about 0.5 F1 on dev; widening the token set to include u/w/s/q raises mass recall to about 0.8 but drops precision to about 0.32.
